materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 1 of "Materials and Making". That is unit 2 in grade 3. Today is a diagnostic probe about drawing tools. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create a small collection of work using at least two different materials or techniques. Today helps by working on drawing tools. Your unit also covers drawing tools, painting or color media, collage basics, and careful tool and material use. Today is for practice. You are scored on finishing and being honest, not on getting it perfect.
primary_task: Before anyone teaches you about drawing tools, make something small. Take a few minutes. Draw a quick sketch, tap a short pattern, or write what you would make. Any of these is fine. Then write three things you already notice about drawing tools. Write one question you cannot answer yet. Keep this. You will look at it again later. This is not judged on how good it is. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about drawing tools. It is part of "Materials and Making". Later days in this unit cover other things, like painting or color media. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about drawing tools; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You may use low-smell, low-dust materials, and you can sit or stand to work. Ask for chunkier handles or grips if that helps.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting drawing tools.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for drawing tools follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for drawing tools, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for drawing tools works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of drawing tools, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking drawing tools mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply drawing tools under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on drawing tools rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
